newsitem.title: FRANCE: France pays tribute to slain Algerian unionist.
newsitem.headline: France pays tribute to slain Algerian unionist.

text.p: France paid tribute on Wednesday to slain Algerian trade union boss Abdelhak Benhamouda, and the main trade unions called a rally in his memory to be held on Thursday.
European Affairs Minister Michel Barnier described Benhamouda as an outstanding unionist and politician.

"He will be sorely missed in the political debate and the quest for a solution," Barnier said in remarks before the National Assembly, adding that his murder on Tuesday in Algiers marked a new stage in Algeria's worsening civil strife.

Barnier repeated the government's rejection of a call for a political initiative on Algeria despite Socialist opposition leader Lionel Jospin's attempt to shake the establishment out of silence on bloodshed in the former North African colony.
"We have repeatedly called for a genuine dialogue and reconciliation which is the condition for restoring peace which depends entirely on the Algerians," he said.
"This does not mean an embarrassed silence or indifference on our part, but merely the recognition that it is a sovereign state," he said.

The main French trade unions said they would stage rallies in Paris and in major cities to pay tribute to Benhamouda and express solidarity with Algerian workers. The head of the CFDT union, Nicole Notat, will attend his funeral in Algiers.
